# Workspace-owned files open as tabs in the workspace strip (and 7 more)

This request comes from a conversation with the developer about their app.
Anything marked suspected or not checked is a guess: confirm it in the code before building on it.

## What this is about
Today every opened file switches the whole main area to one global editor screen (App.tsx:130 onOpened -> setView("editor"), App.tsx:665), which takes the user out of the app they were working in. Wanted: a file under a workspace's root folder (deepest root wins, the existing ownerOf rule) opens as a tab in that workspace's own tab strip next to its terminals, with no editor side pane. Files under no workspace stay in the global editor view. The same feature also adds a right-click context menu to the explorer (including 'Reveal in File Explorer' and 'Open terminal here'), and renames App/Project to Workspace everywhere: UI, code, tinkerdeck.json (with a v1 to v2 migration) and the tdk CLI/MCP.

## What to build or fix

### 1. Workspace-owned files open as tabs in the workspace strip (confirmed)
Ownership is by path: a file belongs to the workspace whose root folder contains its path, and the deepest root wins. This is the existing ownerOf in src/state/editorGroups.ts:9-23; reuse it unchanged. Opening a file that a workspace owns, from anywhere (explorer, Ctrl+O, tdk, etc.), switches to that workspace and selects the file's tab in its tab strip (src/features/terminals/TabStrip.tsx), next to the terminals and the Console tab group. It no longer switches the main view to the global editor (today App.tsx:130 useEditor({ onOpened: () => setView("editor") })). Required behaviour:
- Each workspace has ONE selected tab, which can be a terminal/console or an editor file. Today a workspace remembers only selectedTerminalId and the editor has one global editor.activeId, so this needs a unified per-workspace selection.
- Inside a workspace the editor has NO vertical side pane. Today that pane is the grouped 'Open editors' tablist (EditorView.tsx:125-157). File tabs live only in the workspace strip.
- On an editor tab the strip's Start/Stop/Restart buttons (TabStrip.tsx:67-77, App.tsx:713-723) are replaced by the editor actions: Save, Save as, Raw/Preview (today EditorView.tsx:61-82). The editor status bar (language/EOL/encoding, EditorView.tsx:160-213) stays with the editor tab.
- File tabs show dirty state and close like today's editor tabs. Closing follows the existing editor rules: unsaved changes are kept, and the Bin stays global.
- Keep exactly ONE CodeSurface instance, lazily loaded via React.lazy (EditorView.tsx:12, CodeSurface.tsx:1-2), for whichever editor tab is visible, whether in a workspace or in the global view. Per-document EditorState stays in the states map (CodeSurface.tsx:40), and the liveIds mechanism (EditorView.tsx:184-193) keeps the other docs' state. Terminals keep staying mounted while hidden (App.tsx:726-753), so switching between a file tab and a terminal tab must not kill or remount terminals.
- Editor shortcuts Ctrl+S/N/O/W are bound on window today while EditorView is mounted (EditorView.tsx:26-43). They must apply only while an editor tab is the active/visible tab. With a terminal tab focused, Ctrl+W/Ctrl+N etc. must go to the terminal, not the editor.
- New (Ctrl+N or button) while inside a workspace creates an unsaved document whose 'home' is that workspace. Without this it would go to Misc, because unsaved docs have no path (editorGroups.ts:33-42). The home is remembered until the first save; after that the path decides.
- Tabs move deliberately when ownership changes: Save as into or out of a workspace folder, rename/move through the explorer (explorer commands already re-point or close affected tabs, useExplorerOps.ts:36-38), a workspace root change, or a workspace deletion. The tab moves to its new home (another workspace strip or the global view) with its content, dirty state and undo intact. Nothing is lost.

- BRS-app-launcher.md:356 (7.14 Organisation)

- developer: 'when editor is open within a workspace, it should not be accompanies by the sidepane'

### 2. Global editor view holds only files that belong to no workspace (confirmed)
The header Editor button (App.tsx:573-574, toggles main view between 'home' and 'editor') keeps opening the global editor view. That view now lists ONLY files owned by no workspace (today's Misc group) plus unsaved docs that have no workspace home. Workspace-owned files never appear there: a file is in exactly one strip, never two. Grouping is not needed in this view; show a plain list/strip of the unowned files. Opening an unowned file opens this view and selects it. The Bin stays global.

- developer: 'Only files that belong to no app (today's Misc)'

### 3. Explorer right-click context menu (confirmed)
Add a context menu to the explorer tree (src/features/explorer/ExplorerPanel.tsx) using @radix-ui/react-context-menu (new dependency). It is unstyled; style it only with the existing theme CSS variables (--panel, --panel-2, --border, --hover, --text, --muted, --accent, --shadow, --radius in src/styles/global.css:1-41) so that it follows data-theme dark/light. Radix handles flip/shift at window edges, submenus, keyboard navigation, typeahead, Escape/click-outside closing and focus return. cmdk (package.json:28) already pulls in Radix base packages, so the added cost should be small, but this has not been measured: check the vite build output after adding it. Entries:
- File: Open, Reveal in File Explorer, Copy path, Copy relative path (relative to the owning workspace root; for unowned files, decide sensibly, e.g. relative to the explorer root), Rename, Move, Delete.
- Folder: New file, New folder, Reveal in File Explorer, Open terminal here (see separate item; hidden when no workspace owns the folder), Copy path, Rename, Move, Delete.
- Empty area of the tree: New file, New folder, Refresh, Show/Hide hidden files.
The menu opens on right-click and also with Shift+F10 or the Menu key on the focused tree item. F2 (rename) and Del (delete) work as shortcuts on the focused item. Rename/Move/Delete/New reuse the existing toolbar ops and backend commands explorer_create/rename/move/delete (src-tauri/src/features/explorer/commands.rs:42,134,149,164), which already re-point or close affected editor tabs (useExplorerOps.ts:36-38). The toolbar (ExplorerPanel.tsx:354-396) stays. There is no context menu anywhere in src/ today.

### 4. Backend command: reveal a path in File Explorer (confirmed)
Add a new Tauri command that reveals an arbitrary file or folder in Windows File Explorer by running explorer.exe /select,<path>. The only existing shell-out is open_config_folder, which opens the config dir only. Use it for the menu's 'Reveal in File Explorer'. Pass the path as a separate argument (no shell string building), and validate that the path exists.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/commands.rs:205-212 open_config_folder (only explorer.exe use)

### 5. 'Open terminal here' opens a Console instance in the owning workspace (confirmed)
On a folder, 'Open terminal here' opens a NEW Console instance in the workspace that owns the folder (ownerOf, deepest root wins). It starts in the clicked folder and is selected in that workspace's strip; the app switches to that workspace first if needed. It is temporary and is NOT saved to the config (users who want to keep it add a terminal in the workspace Edit pane as today). It is hidden for folders under no workspace, because the global view has no terminals. Today console instances have ids console-<appId>:<n>:<shell> and always start in the root: console_def_with_id hard-codes cwd "." and command "" (model.rs:227-235), resolved against app.root (commands.rs:51-55). The console instance must carry its start folder the way it already carries its shell, instead of the hard-coded ".". Keep the folder relative to the workspace root, or validate it stays inside the root. The shell used is the default console shell (powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, cmd.exe, gitbash, wsl.exe are supported, mcp.rs:29). Any id format change must keep existing console ids parsing.

### 6. Rename App/Project to Workspace in UI and code (confirmed)
Use 'Workspace' as the single term everywhere in the UI and code: UI text, component/file names, identifiers, types and state (e.g. SidebarProjects, AppDef, apps, selectedTerminalId per app, editorGroups 'app' naming, save_apps command and its frontend calls), tests, and the BRS doc where it names the concept. A grep of \bProjects?\b|\bWorkspaces?\b over src/*.tsx gave 116 matches in 10 files (Sidebar.tsx, SidebarProjects.tsx, SidebarTabs.tsx, EditPane.tsx, ExplorerPanel.tsx, tests), and 'app' is used throughout frontend and backend. Where 'app' means Tinkerdeck itself (e.g. 'restarts the app'), it stays. User-facing config messages such as 'Your saved apps…' (config.rs:86,96,107) become 'workspaces'. All new UI text from this feature says 'workspace'.

Evidence:
- grep \bProjects?\b|\bWorkspaces?\b in src/*.tsx: 116 occurrences in 10 files
- src-tauri/src/model.rs:121 pub apps: Vec<AppDef>

- developer: 'we need to cannonize from App/Project to Workspace'; 'ok but include workspace rename in this feature'

### 7. tinkerdeck.json v2 with 'workspaces' and migration from v1 (confirmed)
Bump CONFIG_VERSION from 1 to 2 (model.rs:6). In v2 the top-level key `apps` becomes `workspaces` (model.rs:121); rename the inner fields too where they say 'app'. Loading: parse() checks the version before deserialising (config.rs:48-59). A v1 file is read as before and converted to v2 in memory. It is written as v2 on the next normal save, and the save keeps the previous file as .bak, so the v1 copy survives. A file with version > 2 stays TooNew as today. Consequence by design: once written as v2, an older Tinkerdeck build refuses the file with its existing 'newer version' message and will not save over it (config.rs:92-98). The migration is one-way. Add tests: v1 file loads into the same workspaces; the first save writes v2 plus .bak; a v2 round-trip works; v3 is rejected as TooNew.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/model.rs:6 CONFIG_VERSION = 1
- src-tauri/src/model.rs:121 pub apps: Vec<AppDef>
- src-tauri/src/config.rs:10 FILE_NAME = tinkerdeck.json
- src-tauri/src/config.rs:48-59 version checked first; > CONFIG_VERSION -> TooNew
- src-tauri/src/config.rs:92-98 TooNew locks with 'newer version' message
- developer: 'Everything, including tinkerdeck.json and the tdk CLI, with a migration'

### 8. Rename app to workspace in the tdk CLI and MCP server (confirmed)
In tdk: the help/usage text (<app> -> <workspace>, cli.rs:43-82), the RPC method names sent to Tinkerdeck (app.add, app.detect, app.up/down and app.{cmd}, cli.rs:185,192,197 -> workspace.*), their JSON params ({"app": ...} -> {"workspace": ...}), the matching RPC handlers in the app, and the MCP tool arguments/descriptions (mcp.rs, 48 uses of 'app', e.g. mcp.rs:325 arguments { "app": "Shop" }). Workspace arguments stay positional, so scripts like `tdk up Shop` keep working. tdk and the app ship together, so the RPC names change in step and no old-name aliases are planned (see open question). Where 'app' means Tinkerdeck itself (cli.rs:73 'restarts the app'), keep it. Also check src-tauri/src/bin/tdk/register.rs for 'app' wording.

Evidence:
- src-tauri/src/bin/tdk/cli.rs:43-82 usage text with <app>
- src-tauri/src/bin/tdk/cli.rs:185,192,197 call("app.{cmd}"/"app.add"/"app.detect", json!({"app": ...}))
- src-tauri/src/bin/tdk/cli.rs:73 'restarts the app' = Tinkerdeck
- src-tauri/src/bin/tdk/mcp.rs: 48 occurrences of app; mcp.rs:325
- src-tauri/src/bin/tdk/register.rs
- src-tauri/src/bin/tdk/client.rs only RPC client found in repo

## Not part of this
- Split views (editor beside a terminal)
- Dragging tabs between workspaces or between a workspace and the global view
- Chunked/streamed file loading. Files stay read whole with the 5 MB edit cap (src-tauri/src/editor.rs:11, 75-87); CodeMirror already renders only visible lines. A read-only large-file viewer could be a separate issue later
- Saving an 'Open terminal here' console as a permanent workspace terminal (users add terminals through the Edit pane as today)
- Terminals in the global editor view

## Not settled yet (do not treat as fact)
- Assumed, not verified: nothing outside this repo calls Tinkerdeck's RPC with the old 'app.*' method names except tdk, so no aliases are kept. This is wrong if another tool or script talks to the RPC directly; if so, keep the old names as aliases.
- The added bundle size of @radix-ui/react-context-menu has not been measured; check the vite build output after adding it.
- 'Copy relative path' for files under no workspace: relative to what was not discussed. Suggested default: the explorer's current root.

## Requirements agreed in the conversation

The developer and the assistant already agreed these while talking. Build on them; do not ask again what they settle.

- **R1**: An editor for a file that belongs to a registered workspace is hosted as a tab in that workspace's tab strip alongside the workspace's terminal tabs, and the workspace view stays on screen.
  - Done when: Opening a file under a workspace's root folder shows an editor tab in that workspace's tab strip while the workspace's terminal tabs remain visible.
  - Done when: Selecting the editor tab shows the file; selecting a terminal tab returns to that terminal without the workspace view being replaced.
  - Done when: The workspace's tab strip contains editor tabs and terminal tabs at the same time.
- **R2**: Editors for files that belong to no registered workspace are kept in a global editor view's tab strip, separate from any workspace's tab strip. The global strip lists only these unowned files, corresponding to today's Misc group.
  - Done when: Opening a file outside every workspace root shows it in the global tab strip.
  - Done when: That editor does not appear in any workspace's tab strip.
  - Done when: The global tab strip lists only files that belong to no workspace.
- **R3**: A file belongs to the workspace whose root folder contains the file's path. When more than one registered workspace's root contains the path, the deepest root wins.
  - Done when: A file anywhere under a workspace's root folder is treated as belonging to that workspace.
  - Done when: A file under two nested workspace roots is treated as belonging to the deeper workspace.
  - Done when: A file outside every workspace root belongs to no workspace.
- **R4**: Each open editor appears in exactly one strip: a file owned by a workspace only in its owning workspace's tab strip, and a file that belongs to no workspace only in the global tab strip. No file appears in both strips.
  - Done when: An editor for a workspace-owned file is absent from the global tab strip.
  - Done when: An editor for an unowned file is absent from every workspace's tab strip.
  - Done when: Opening the same file does not create a second copy in another strip.
- **R5**: Inside a workspace, the editor is shown without the side pane that lists or groups open editors by owner; the workspace's own tab strip is the only tab list there. The global editor view still lists only unowned files, as a plain list with no grouping.
  - Done when: Opening a file in a workspace shows the editor without the vertical 'Open editors' list that groups editors by owner.
  - Done when: The editor tab sits in the workspace's tab strip, and selecting it shows the file.
  - Done when: The global editor view shows a plain list of unowned files with no grouping.
- **R6**: There is a single editor instance, loaded lazily: editor code is not loaded until a file is first opened, and the same one editor surface shows whichever editor tab is visible, whether in a workspace or in the global view.
  - Done when: Before the first file is opened, the editor code is not loaded.
  - Done when: Opening a second file reuses the existing editor surface instead of creating another.
  - Done when: Switching from a workspace editor tab to another editor tab or to the global view shows the selected file in the same editor surface.
- **R7**: The registered-app concept is renamed to Workspace everywhere: user-facing labels and messages, the saved configuration file, the tdk command-line tool and its MCP tool arguments, and internal code identifiers all use Workspace instead of App or Project, with matching plural and possessive forms. Where 'app' means Tinkerdeck itself (for example 'restarts the app'), that wording stays.
  - Done when: User-facing labels and messages for registered apps say Workspace, not App or Project; plural and possessive forms read Workspaces and Workspace's.
  - Done when: The saved configuration uses a workspaces key in place of an apps key.
  - Done when: tdk help text, its positional arguments and its MCP tool arguments say workspace; scripts that pass the workspace as a positional argument, such as 'tdk up Shop', keep working.
  - Done when: The editor-tab and context-menu text introduced by this feature uses the same Workspace wording.
- **R8**: Right-clicking a file or folder in the explorer opens a context menu with common file operations: files offer Reveal in File Explorer, Rename and Delete; folders offer New file, New folder, Reveal in File Explorer, Rename, Delete and, when the folder belongs to a workspace, Open terminal here (R10).
  - Done when: Right-clicking a file shows a menu with Reveal in File Explorer, Rename and Delete.
  - Done when: Right-clicking a folder shows a menu with New file, New folder, Reveal in File Explorer, Rename and Delete.
  - Done when: Choosing an action performs the same result as the existing explorer toolbar action of the same name.
  - Done when: Reveal in File Explorer opens the operating system's file manager with the item selected.
- **R9**: The saved configuration file moves to version 2, where a workspaces key replaces apps. A version 1 file is read as before and converted in memory, and is written as version 2 on the next save while the previous file is kept as a .bak. An older Tinkerdeck that opens a version 2 file refuses it with its existing 'written by a newer version' message and does not overwrite it.
  - Done when: A version 1 configuration containing an apps list loads and its entries appear as workspaces.
  - Done when: After the next save the file is version 2 with a workspaces key and no apps key.
  - Done when: The previous configuration is retained as a .bak file.
  - Done when: A version 2 file opened by an older build is refused with the existing newer-version message and is not overwritten.
- **R10**: Right-clicking a folder inside a workspace offers 'Open terminal here', which opens a new Console instance in the workspace that owns that folder (the deepest matching root), so the new console appears in that workspace's tab strip.
  - Done when: Right-clicking a folder inside a workspace shows an 'Open terminal here' item.
  - Done when: Choosing it opens a new Console instance in that workspace's tab strip.
  - Done when: With nested workspaces the console is created in the deeper workspace that owns the folder.

findings.description: Opening the global editor view while a workspace editor tab is remembered and an unowned tab is open never settles: the workspace effect keeps reselecting the workspace-owned file and the global effect reselects the unowned one, so the global strip never stays on an unowned tab (A2) and the app spins, re-rendering and hammering editor.select/api.touch/localStorage. Gate the workspace sync on the workspace main area actually being shown (view === 'app'), or give editor.activeId a single owner.
findings.evidence: App's workspace sync effect (src/App.tsx:361-363) runs whenever onWorkspaceEditor is true, regardless of view, and calls editor.select(workspaceTabId). GlobalEditorView's effect (src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:166-168) calls editor.select(shownId) for the first unowned tab. Both are mounted while view === 'editor'. Reproduced with a probe: open a workspace-owned file, select its tab, then open the global Editor view with one unowned tab open -> the two effects alternate select(E)/select(U) forever (uncaught 'LOOP-LIMIT reached: 41 selection touches'; without the guard the test hangs).
findings.note: confirmed by the whole Challenge after being settled without a Build (The workspace selection effect is now gated on the workspace view actually being shown: src/App.tsx:364 `if (view === "app" && onWorkspaceEditor && workspaceTabId && activeDocId !== workspaceTabId) selectDoc(workspaceTabId)`, so it cannot run while the global editor view is mounted. GlobalEditorView keeps the only writer there (src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:166-168). The added SEC-1 test (src/App.editor.test.tsx:262-285) selects a workspace file, opens the global view with an unowned tab and asserts the unowned tab is selected and a.ts is absent; it passes, and the full targeted run (155 tests, 7 files) passed.)

findings.evidence: The workspace branch (src/App.tsx:763-887) renders TabStrip, TerminalHosts and EditorSurface but never renders editor.error; EditorSurface only shows the active doc's a.error (src/features/editor/EditorSurface.tsx:75), and the only editor.error renders are in the global view (src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:212, old :67). Probe: inside a workspace, a rejected open of a 'too large' file leaves both role=alert and the 'too large' text null while the workspace stays on screen.

The added REV-2/R1 test (src/App.editor.test.tsx:227-245) opens a rejected 'too large' file inside the Qonsol workspace and asserts the too-large message is shown, the workspace stays on screen, no editor tab is created, and Dismiss clears it; it passes. findings.description: Infinite render/update loop (unbounded work, CPU and memory burn, UI becomes unresponsive and React aborts with a max-update-depth error) when the global editor view is shown while a workspace editor tab is still the remembered selection. Gate the App workspace-selection effect on view === "app" (or clear editorSelection when entering the global view / on route to an unowned file) so the two selection effects can never disagree.
findings.evidence: The workspace-selection effect at src/App.tsx:361-363 is not gated on the current view: whenever a workspace editor tab is remembered it calls selectDoc(workspaceTabId) even while view === "editor". GlobalEditorView adds a competing effect at src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:166-168 that calls select(shownId) whenever the active document is not one of the unowned tabs. With a workspace-owned tab selected (it was opened via openPath, so editorSelection[app.id] points at it) and any unowned tab open, entering the global view makes both effects write different ids to editor.activeId on every commit: App selects the workspace tab, GlobalEditorView selects the unowned tab, forever. Reproduced against the current code with a probe test: React reports "Maximum update depth exceeded ... at App (src/App.tsx:83)" and the commits never settle, each one re-running partitionTabs/groupTabs over every open tab and every workspace. Reachable by opening a workspace file (which sets the remembered selection) then opening an unowned file from the command palette (route sets view to "editor" without clearing editorSelection), or by opening a workspace file and then pressing the header Editor button while an unowned tab is already open.
findings.note: src/App.tsx:363-365 now gates the workspace-selection effect on view === "app" (view added to its dependency list), so it cannot write editor.activeId while GlobalEditorView is mounted; GlobalEditorView's own select effect (src/features/editor/EditorView.tsx:166-168) is therefore the only one active in the global view and the two can no longer ping-pong. With a remembered workspace tab plus an open unowned tab, entering the global view settles on the unowned tab: the SEC-1 regression test at src/App.editor.test.tsx:194-217 passes (npx vitest run src/App.editor.test.tsx -t "SEC-1": 1 passed), asserting the unowned tab is selected, the workspace tab is absent, and the surface shows the unowned file. The effect now stops once activeDocId === workspaceTabId because select is a stable useCallback.
